_meta.title: Qwen3.7-Max blog ingest + AA Intelligence Index (qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.7, May 20 2026)
_meta.context: Alibaba Qwen Team published Qwen3.7-Max as 'the Agent Frontier' on 2026-05-20. Positioned as a frontier coding agent foundation: frontend prototyping → complex SWE; office productivity + workflow automation via MCP and multi-agent orchestration; sustained autonomous execution on long-horizon tasks; cross-scaffold generalization. Blog publishes a comprehensive 41-benchmark × 6-model comparison table (Opus-4.6 Max / K2.6 Thinking / GLM-5.1 Thinking / DS-V4-Pro Max / Qwen3.6-Plus / Qwen3.7-Max). AA listed AAII = 57 with the disclaimer 'Results claimed by AI Lab (not yet independently verified)' — confirms the blog is the canonical primary source, AA simply re-displays Qwen's self-reported values. Prior DB state for Qwen3.7-Max: only 1 score (arena.ai text Elo 1475 from Session 19 ingest).
_meta.rule: STRICT-ATTRIBUTION + PRESERVATION. Qwen3.7-Max is the target model — ALL 41 published benchmark cells ingested where != '--'. For OTHER models in the comparison column, preserve existing DB primary-source data: skip cross-vendor ingest for PUBLIC benchmarks (Terminal Bench, SWE-*, GPQA, HLE, MMLU-*, LiveCodeBench, HMMT, MRCR etc.) since Anthropic/Moonshot/Zhipu/DeepSeek/Alibaba each have their own canonical first-party sources for their models on these. ONLY cross-model ingest the 7 NEW Qwen-internal benchmarks (QwenWebDev, QwenSVG, Qwenclaw, CoWorkBench, Vitabench, SpreadSheetBench-v1, QwenWorldBench) where the Qwen blog IS the primary source for every model in the panel — no conflict possible. Skip Qwen3.6-Plus on these too since DB already has 47 prior primary-source scores. Variant ambiguity: Qwen labels 'Opus-4.6 Max' / 'K2.6 Thinking' / 'GLM-5.1 Thinking' / 'DS-V4-Pro Max' — exact reasoning-effort variants not publicly distinguished by those vendors, so attribute to base IDs (claude-opus-4.6, kimi-k2.6, glm-5.1, deepseek-v4-pro-max) with a _note documenting the Qwen-published qualifier. Kernel Bench L3 cells like '2.63/98%' are dual-metric (speedup geomean × pass rate %) — ingest only the pass-rate component (98%) as kernelbench_l3.

benchmarks.name: QwenWebDev
benchmarks.description: Qwen-team internal frontend-code-generation benchmark. Bilingual (Chinese/English) prompts requesting full HTML/JS/CSS pages. Scored on Elo arena vs reference solutions. arxiv pending; first appeared in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: QwenSVG
benchmarks.description: Qwen-team internal SVG generation benchmark. Tests vector-graphics code generation from natural-language descriptions. Scored on Elo arena. First published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: Qwenclaw
benchmarks.description: Qwen-team internal Claude-Code-style coding-agent benchmark. Tests an agent's ability to navigate codebases, edit files, run commands, and complete software-engineering tasks end-to-end. Scored on success rate (%). First published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: CoWorkBench
benchmarks.description: Qwen-team internal multi-agent coworking benchmark. Tests cooperation between multiple agent instances on shared workflows (planning, hand-off, parallel sub-tasks). Scored on completion rate (%). First published Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: Vitabench
benchmarks.description: Life-tasks benchmark — long-horizon personal-assistant tasks (travel planning, household coordination, etc.). Published via Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20. Possibly third-party with Qwen as the eval host.

benchmarks.name: SpreadSheetBench v1
benchmarks.description: Spreadsheet-manipulation agent benchmark. Tests the ability of an agent to navigate, edit, and analyze tabular data via formula authoring and pivot operations. Published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: KernelBench L3 — Pass Rate
benchmarks.description: KernelBench Level-3 (composition of multiple CUDA primitives) — pass rate (%). Cell value 'x.xx/yy%' in Qwen blog represents 'geomean speedup / pass rate %'; we ingest the pass-rate component. The speedup component is a secondary metric we may add later.

benchmarks.name: QwenWorldBench
benchmarks.description: Qwen-team internal world-knowledge/multi-domain reasoning benchmark. Scored as accuracy (%). First published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: MAXIFE
benchmarks.description: Multilingual extreme instruction-following eval — extension of IFEval to many languages. Published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-ProX
benchmarks.description: MMLU-Pro extended to non-English locales — translated and re-validated questions across additional languages. Published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: NOVA-63
benchmarks.description: 63-language coverage benchmark assessing multilingual knowledge + reasoning. Published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.

benchmarks.name: PolyMATH
benchmarks.description: Multilingual mathematics benchmark — translated math problems across multiple languages. Published in Qwen3.7-Max launch blog 2026-05-20.
